sentences.text: Ruthenibacterium lactatiformans, the species for which this genus was named, was isolated from the faeces of healthy human subjects as a Gram-stain-negative, rod-shaped, obligately anaerobic bacterium.
It ferments glucose with d-lactic acid, succinic acid and acetic acid as end products, and was placed in a new genus within the family Ruminococcaceae.
A case report described bacteraemia and potential vertebral osteomyelitis caused by Ruthenibacterium lactatiformans, reported as the first documented human infection with this organism.
A study of adolescents reported the genus Ruthenibacterium to be more abundant in controls with normal weight than in participants with overweight.
